chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Exalted is His Mention,
and fear Allah, by Whom you are asking by Him and the kinship; surely Allah was Ever-Watchful over you.
So he said: These are the relationships of the people. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Commanded with their goodly maintenance, and magnified them. Do you not see that He Made it to be from Him?
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'and the kinship' (wal-arham) refer to in Surah An-Nisa?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the 'al-arham' mentioned in the verse refers to the general kinship ties of humanity, emphasizing that Allah commanded their maintenance and magnified their status by linking them directly to His own name. This interpretation underscores the theological weight of silat al-rahim, positioning it not merely as a social courtesy but as a divine obligation intrinsically connected to God's presence and watchfulness. The hadith serves as a foundational proof in Shia jurisprudence for the obligatory nature of maintaining family bonds, derived from the grammatical structure of the verse where kinship is conjoined with the name of Allah.
